q1_findLiveHost.answer: The shared CampaignHostRegistry is the only lookup that reaches the live host from the API graph in every process history; coopHostRegistry.activeHosts is not usable.
evidence: CampaignHostRegistry keys entries by matchId (:254) and has no campaignId lookup; the least code is a scan method on the registry (entries whose campaignId matches and whose host is not closed), estimated +12 lines.

activeHosts is populated in the graph whose CampaignHostRegistry class built the slot instance (register :321 calls that graph's registerActiveCoopHost), so which graph holds the host depends on who called getCampaignHostRegistry first (the create route in a fresh process, the socket binder after a restart).
Measured live (baseline, port 24961): the socket graph's coopHostRegistry module is loaded and its getActiveCoopHost(campaignId) returns undefined at S0-S3 while the shared slot holds the live entry.

Measured in the build (.next/server/pages/api/multiplayer/matches.js): the API graph's copy of coopHostRegistry is tree-shaken to one export (py = registerActiveCoopHost: `let h=new Map;function g(a){return h.set(a.campaignId,a),()=>{h.get(a.campaignId)===a&&h.delete(a.campaignId)}}`); getActiveCoopHost is absent, so the API graph map has no reader and its contents were not read.

q2_applyOrRefuse.answer: Neither branch can be delivered inside the unit's paths without breaking the co-op host's day advance; admission stops BLOCKED.
q2_applyOrRefuse.apply: No host operation adopts a whole state: openLocked commits a snapshot only on an empty log (doors.ts:86-106, :94) and no intent carries a whole state (CampaignSync.ts:432-438, :529). Applying a PUT through the host needs a new host door committing a CampaignSnapshotPublished from the envelope projection, plus a row write for the envelope fields the host state does not hold, outside the one journal transaction that writes the row today (campaignRecordJournalSave.ts:86-145); diffing the envelope into intents is the transformer the doctrine forbids. INFERENCE (not run): it also double-advances the day, because the host client PUTs the advanced campaign and then sends AdvanceDay {days: 1} (dayActions.ts:239-247, :350-354), which the host computes as newDay = state.day + days (CampaignMatchHostIntent.ts:236-241) from the day the adopted PUT already advanced.
q2_applyOrRefuse.refuse: The refusal is the least server code (estimated route +40, registry +12) and keeps the host the single writer, but the co-op host client routes its own actions through that PUT before (or instead of) a host command. Measured with the real campaign store and persistence store (scratch probe, fetch stubbed per row): answered 200 (the baseline answer while live), advanceDay returns a report and sends one AdvanceDay host intent {days: 1}; answered the refusal 409 in the typed conflict shape, advanceDay returns null, sends no host intent, rolls the date back and toasts "Co-op campaign save was refused: the campaign changed elsewhere. Your local change was rolled back." With a host entry present for the whole process (entries are never disposed or closed outside tests), the host could not advance the day, travel, or apply any updateCampaign change on a co-op campaign once its session was created. e2e/coop-campaign-two-browser-journey.spec.ts:365-377 drives exactly this host day advance.

trade.fixAssessment: The root cause is two writers of one co-op campaign: the host client lands its own ledger changes through the whole-envelope PUT checkpoint and only then (advanceDay) or never (travel, updateCampaign) sends a host command. The route cannot remove the second writer alone: refusing strands those client flows, adopting double-counts the day.
trade.removed: Nothing removed; no product edit made. A campaignId index inside the registry was considered and rejected for a scan (the entries are the process live co-op sessions).
trade.scope: A successor needs src/stores/campaign/useCampaignStore.dayActions.ts (advanceDayAction :239-247, finishCoopAdvanceDay :306-318, travelToSystemAction :377-382) and src/stores/campaign/useCampaignStore.actions.ts (:259-263, :286-290) so a co-op host with a live session stops routing ledger state through the PUT, plus the route and registry changes; or an owner ruling on which host-client effects become host commands.

A live host means registered and not closed. In production no code path disposes or closes a campaign entry (dispose and hostDisconnected have no non-test callers), so after a co-op match is created every PUT of that campaign would be refused for the life of the process.

findings: FN-u96-coop-host-client-routes-ledger-through-put (measured, clientProbe): the co-op host client saves its own day advance, travel and updateCampaign changes through the whole-envelope PUT and, for the day, sends AdvanceDay only after that PUT commits; any server-side refusal or adoption of that PUT while live changes those flows.

FN-u96-campaign-host-entries-never-disposed (read): CampaignHostRegistry.dispose (:390-395) and CampaignSyncSession.hostDisconnected (:795-799) have no non-test callers, so a campaign host entry lives until process exit; "a live host exists" then means "a co-op match was created for this campaign in this process".

FN-u96-day-effects-ride-the-checkpoint (INFERENCE, the same mechanism as the measured erasure): the day pipeline's non-day effects on a co-op host reach the journal only through the PUT checkpoint (AdvanceDay carries newDay only), so the next host command's absolute FundsChanged balance erases a checkpointed balance change as it erased 382500.

The specs are silent on a whole-campaign save while a live host holds the campaign (coop-campaign-sync Host-as-GM :215-217 names the host the single write authority; campaign-persistence :111-128 defines only the baseVersion 409); the ruling should land as a spec delta.
